items.title: When AI builds itself
items.description: Anthropic's own account of AI starting to automate AI research, and why recursive self-improvement is the thing they say they are now watching most closely.

items.title: Writing is Thinking
items.description: A Nature editorial on why you should not hand your writing to a model wholesale: the act of writing is where the thinking actually happens, not a chore around it.

items.title: The Kaiser and a "Mediocre Man" Theory of History
description: A case that Wilhelm II mattered precisely because he was mediocre, and that history sometimes turns on the ordinary failings of whoever happens to hold power.

It reminded me of Mark Twain's ["Luck"](https://americanliterature.com/author/mark-twain/short-story/luck), though the two stories work in opposite directions. Twain's fool is carried upward by chance and mistaken for a hero, so the error is in how we read him. The Kaiser is no genius either, yet he really does bend events, so the mediocrity itself is the cause.

items.title: Nobody Ever Gets Credit for Fixing Problems that Never Happened
items.author: Repenning & Sterman
items.description: The classic systems paper on why organizations get stuck firefighting: fixing root causes is invisible, so the work that prevents crises is never the work that gets rewarded.

items.title: A backdoor in a LinkedIn job offer
items.description: A developer walks through a fake recruiter's "coding task" that would have run a remote backdoor on `npm install`. A tidy anatomy of a social-engineered supply-chain attack.

items.title: Has AI Already Killed How-To Nonfiction?
items.description: Tim Ferriss shows his own catalog's sales falling off a cliff as models commoditize how-to information, and argues the survivors will sell transformation and community rather than facts.

items.title: 1,000 True Fans
items.author: Kevin Kelly
items.description: The essay that keeps getting more relevant: you do not need millions, just a thousand people who will buy whatever you make. Read it next to the Ferriss piece above.

items.title: The Wholesale Plagiarism of Obscure Sorrows
items.author: Andy Baio
items.description: An agency AI-cloned John Koenig's entire Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows into a slicker, better-ranked site and monetized it. The new shape of plagiarism.

items.title: Why Coding Is Solved, and What Comes Next
items.author: Boris Cherny
items.description: The Claude Code lead argues the bottleneck has moved off writing code and onto everything around it: taste, review, and deciding what to build.

items.title: Coding is no longer the constraint: scaling devex to teams and agents
items.description: How a large org rebuilds its developer platform once both humans and agents are shipping code, and coding stops being the thing that limits you.

items.title: How Lovable vibecodes production software at scale
items.description: A look inside how one of the fastest-growing AI products actually ships, from prompt to production.

items.title: Stanford Leadership Forum 2026: a conversation with Ken Griffin
items.author: Ken Griffin
items.description: The Citadel founder on markets, talent, and the long work of building an institution.

items.title: We Need an International Treaty to Ban Superintelligence
items.author: Andrea Miotti
items.description: A case for a verifiable international ban on building superintelligence, on the nuclear-nonproliferation model, while monitoring the compute is still feasible and the window is still open.

items.title: Half-Baked Product
items.description: A parable of an oven startup that bolts on feature after feature to chase every sale while never fixing its core algorithm. On quietly trading the mission for short-term revenue.

items.title: My Antichrist Lecture
items.author: Scott Alexander
items.description: We were discussing with friends how the world feels like it is accelerating toward something, the way technology did in the run-up to WWII, which got me wondering whether there is any resemblance between AI and the Antichrist. To my surprise, the first result when I searched on Google was a Scott Alexander blog post (which I assume is satirical) on similarities between Anthropic and the Antichrist.

items.title: Your New Personal Website Is a Few Prompts Away
items.description: How this site was rebuilt without learning the framework it runs on, by focusing on the look and letting the agent handle the rest.

items.title: Vercel Eve: A Guide
items.description: Notes from building a small demo agent on Vercel Eve: project layout, the dev TUI, tools and skills, scheduling, channels and deployment.

items.title: Sakana Fugu: Multi-Agent Orchestration Explained in Detail
items.description: A guided tour of the two engines behind Sakana's Fugu, the evolved TRINITY router and the RL-trained Conductor, with interactive diagrams of both.

items.title: Building a Local Data Platform on Kubernetes
items.description: A series on building an end-to-end data platform on one k3d cluster on a laptop: streaming ingest, the right storage shape per access pattern, observability and resilience.
